lens.message:
Here's the shift: every Meridian deployment is now gated — nothing ships to staging or production without a signed release manifest. Two unsigned artifacts reached staging last quarter, and that's the whole reason, so verification now happens before shipping rather than after. It changes how we approach Meridian deploys, release sign-off, and what counts as a shippable artifact.

Before/after, on the decision record itself. As written: "Gate: signed release manifest required for Meridian deploys. Scope: applies to staging and production. Owner: Quinton Fairweather." — minutes from 2026-07-02. As it reads now: the operating rule every deploy is checked against — an unsigned artifact is a blocked artifact, the signed manifest is the proof of verification, and Quinton owns the gate.

Right lens?

What it moves: honestly, just the one document so far — this decision record is the only thing indexed on this stream, and I won't pad the list. Runbooks, release-train notes, and staging/production checklists aren't in view yet, but any deploy instructions without a manifest-signing step will read as contradicting the gate once they are.

Want me to apply this across the deployment and release docs as they come into view — or correct it here first?
